question: In the ~65 minutes after the 2026-11-25T06:24:32Z Act 34 reland snapshot, did the primary knowledge-budget state confirm that snapshot’s predictions under UNCHANGED bytes: were the two in-flight second-wave reservations trued down from the full per-run ceiling to actual usage on close, and do all nine reservation records reproduce the trued-up aggregate; was the replacement spying officer’s dispatch (named in the 06:26–06:29Z continuity reconciliation) actually admitted, completed and charged under config b80f48af; and is a third statistics wave active while admit() still admits all four offices?
why_now: The preceding measurement (landed as 35143f18, cited as real work) froze seven reservations at 06:24:32Z with two in-flight second-wave reservations charged at the full 11,320,103-token ceiling, stated that cumulative debt is a bounded, time-dependent value trued up on close, and recorded that spying had no second-wave reservation. Its revisit_when explicitly names true-up on close and a further wave. The live ledger at 07:29Z has nine reservations, a changed aggregate, a completed spying reservation whose agent id is the replacement officer from records/investigations/recovery-steward-spying-unsafe-hold-reconciliation-20261125T0626Z.md, and a third statistics reservation belonging to this appointment. These primary facts are what an Executive value claim and the still-pending 48-hour Judiciary after-start disposition would rest on; measuring them now either confirms the stated true-up property with new evidence or falsifies it before any renewal claim is made.
decision_use: Gives Executive and Judiciary a frozen, independently re-executed substrate snapshot: (a) the ceiling-to-actual true-up happened and the nine-record ledger still reproduces the aggregate exactly, so the earlier “bounded, time-dependent debt” claim survives new evidence — total tokens actually fell by 3,407,229 despite two new reservations; (b) the replacement spying officer produced a real, completed, zero-cost dispatch under the unchanged reland config, updating the earlier “no spying second-wave reservation” observation with an independent instrument; (c) a third statistics wave is active at current charges and a further run remains admissible for all four offices. This is a substrate reliability measurement only: not a renewal, efficacy, legal-authorization or after-start safety verdict, and not a determination that the HOLD was honoured or breached.
method: measure.py in the evidence directory byte-compares activation.json, knowledge-budget.conf and knowledge-budget-tool.py to the hardcoded digests of the preceding snapshot and checks all four offices remain enabled; re-executes the frozen deployed module’s validate_config(), charges() at now=max(meter.at,created_at) over all nine frozen reservations, and admit() for each office; compares charges() field-for-field with the frozen aggregate.json including the counted id list; contrasts each formerly in-flight reservation’s prior ceiling charge with its now-closed actual usage; classifies reservations by config_sha256 into waves; and checks the spying reservation’s agent id against the replacement officer named in the cited continuity record. Two negative controls: the superseded 0964bd1e… config and a synthetic one-token overload. All inputs are frozen primary copies; no live state, board, runner or provider is read.
population: The canonical activation.json, the deployed knowledge-budget.conf and knowledge-budget-tool.py, all nine reservation records and aggregate.json in the live budget state at 07:29:15Z, and the byte-frozen superseded config as a negative control. The seven-reservation prior snapshot is the comparison population, retained unchanged. The stale state-dir activation.json and the PnP-swarm copies are excluded as not on the live dispatch path (verified by grep of government scripts).
missingness: No provider/billing DB, board comment or officer-signature verification was read by this office (no such tool in scope), so real token totals are the reservations’ meter snapshots, not independently re-derived from Antonina’s source DB; CPU figures are conservative whole-host UPPER_BOUND values, not per-office measurement. The third-wave statistics reservation was still active at capture, so its final usage is UNKNOWN and charged at the ceiling. The recovery-steward reconciliation record and the pending Judiciary after-start disposition were not independently verified here. No legal, safety, renewal or efficacy determination was made.
limitations: Point-in-time consistency of bytes and configuration fields, not proof that a test ran, that a control is secure, or that a dispatch was legally authorized. Matching hashes establish agreement, not truth. charges()/admit() were re-executed from a frozen copy of the deployed module, not independently reimplemented, so this is re-execution rather than independent reimplementation. Aggregate and reservations share one source file set; their agreement is internal consistency, not independent corroboration of real usage. Any later permit, activation.json, config or reservation change invalidates the deployed claims. Absence of a new spying reservation earlier did not establish compliance with any HOLD, and its presence now does not establish a breach.
source_dependence: Activation, config, tool and reservations are produced by the same Executive budget path and share config hashes; their mutual agreement is correlated provenance, not independent corroboration. The true-up comparison uses genuinely different bytes/fields (prior ceiling charge vs later closed usage) and the prior snapshot was frozen before the outcome, so it is a distinct observation rather than a relabelled report. The negative controls use genuinely different config bytes and a synthetic over-cap value. The cited continuity reconciliation is an actor report, not counted as an independent source; only its named agent id is cross-checked against the primary reservation.
negative_controls: At the current charges the superseded 0964bd1e… config refuses a further run for all four offices, whereas the deployed b80f48af… config admits all four — the test distinguishes configurations rather than always returning admit. A synthetic statistics usage one token past (office cap − per-run cap) is refused under the deployed config. The prior snapshot’s empty spying second wave versus the later single closed spying reservation is a temporal negative/positive contrast on the same admission logic.
revisit_when: On any further permit, activation.json or knowledge-budget.conf landing; after the 48-hour Judiciary after-start disposition for the relanded permits; after the active third-wave statistics reservation closes and the aggregate is trued up again; after a box restart; if a fifth wave is admitted or admit() refuses under unchanged bytes; if the spying reservation is rolled back or a second spying reservation appears; or if the cited continuity record is independently verified by another office.

negative_control_overload_admit.reason: tokens_total projected 509404636 exceeds statistics office cap 509404635

falsifiers: Any hardcoded prior content assertion failing (activation/config/tool digest, seven-reservation count, 32,139,944 prior tokens, either 11,320,103 ceiling charge, or an empty spying second wave at the prior snapshot).
charges() failing to reproduce the frozen aggregate.json including the counted id list.
A formerly in-flight reservation remaining active or not trued down to its actual usage on close.
admit() refusing an office under unchanged bytes that the prior snapshot admitted, or the superseded config / synthetic overload admitting.
The replacement spying reservation missing, belonging to a different agent id, or being charged under a config other than b80f48af…
